title: Invalid Syntax Tree
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidSyntaxTree occurs if an invalid syntax tree is provided
to the type checker. It should never happen.

title: Blank Pkg Name
description:
Official Go type-checker code. BlankPkgName occurs when a package name is the blank identifier "_".

Per the spec:
"The PackageName must not be the blank identifier."

Example:
package _

title: Mismatched Pkg Name
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MismatchedPkgName occurs when a file's package name doesn't match the
package name already established by other files.

title: Invalid Pkg Use
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidPkgUse occurs when a package identifier is used outside of a
selector expression.

Example:
import "fmt"

var _ = fmt

title: Bad Import Path
description: Official Go type-checker code. BadImportPath occurs when an import path is not valid.

title: Broken Import
description:
Official Go type-checker code. BrokenImport occurs when importing a package fails.

Example:
import "amissingpackage"

title: Import C Renamed
description:
Official Go type-checker code. ImportCRenamed occurs when the special import "C" is renamed. "C" is a
pseudo-package, and must not be renamed.

Example:
import _ "C"

title: Unused Import
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnusedImport occurs when an import is unused.

Example:
import "fmt"

func main() {}

title: Invalid Init Cycle
Duplicate Decl
description:
Official Go type-checker code. DuplicateDecl occurs when an identifier is declared multiple times.

Example:
var x = 1
var x = 2

title: Invalid Decl Cycle
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidDeclCycle occurs when a declaration cycle is not valid.

Example:
type S struct {
S
}

Example:
import "unsafe"

type T [unsafe.Sizeof(T{})]int

title: Invalid Type Cycle
description:
Official Go type-checker code. TODO(markfreeman): Retire InvalidTypeCycle, as it's never emitted.

InvalidTypeCycle occurs when a cycle in type definitions results in a
type that is not well-defined.

title: Invalid Const Init
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidConstInit occurs when a const declaration has a non-constant
initializer.

Example:
var x int
const _ = x

title: Invalid Const Val
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidConstVal occurs when a const value cannot be converted to its
target type.

TODO(findleyr): this error code and example are not very clear. Consider
removing it.

Example:
const _ = 1 << "hello"

title: Invalid Const Type
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidConstType occurs when the underlying type in a const declaration
is not a valid constant type.

Example:
const c *int = 4

title: Untyped Nil Use
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UntypedNilUse occurs when the predeclared (untyped) value nil is used to
initialize a variable declared without an explicit type.

Example:
var x = nil

title: Wrong Assign Count
description:
Official Go type-checker code. WrongAssignCount occurs when the number of values on the right-hand side
of an assignment or initialization expression does not match the number
of variables on the left-hand side.

Example:
var x = 1, 2

title: Unassignable Operand
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnassignableOperand occurs when the left-hand side of an assignment is
not assignable.

Example:
func f() {
const c = 1
c = 2
}

title: No New Var
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NoNewVar occurs when a short variable declaration (':=') does not declare
new variables.

Example:
func f() {
x := 1
x := 2
}

title: Multi Val Assign Op
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MultiValAssignOp occurs when an assignment operation (+=, *=, etc) does
not have single-valued left-hand or right-hand side.

Per the spec:
"In assignment operations, both the left- and right-hand expression lists
must contain exactly one single-valued expression"

Example:
func f() int {
x, y := 1, 2
x, y += 1
return x + y
}

title: Invalid Iface Assign
Invalid Chan Assign
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidChanAssign occurs when a chan assignment is invalid.

Per the spec, a value x is assignable to a channel type T if:
"x is a bidirectional channel value, T is a channel type, x's type V and
T have identical element types, and at least one of V or T is not a
defined type."

Example:
type T1 chan int
type T2 chan int

var x T1
// Invalid assignment because both types are named
var _ T2 = x

title: Incompatible Assign
description:
Official Go type-checker code. IncompatibleAssign occurs when the type of the right-hand side expression
in an assignment cannot be assigned to the type of the variable being
assigned.

Example:
var x []int
var _ int = x

title: Unaddressable Field Assign
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnaddressableFieldAssign occurs when trying to assign to a struct field
in a map value.

Example:
func f() {
m := make(map[string]struct{i int})
m["foo"].i = 42
}

title: Not A Type
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NotAType occurs when the identifier used as the underlying type in a type
declaration or the right-hand side of a type alias does not denote a type.

Example:
var S = 2

type T S

title: Invalid Array Len
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidArrayLen occurs when an array length is not a constant value.

Example:
var n = 3
var _ = [n]int{}

title: Blank Iface Method
description:
Official Go type-checker code. BlankIfaceMethod occurs when a method name is '_'.

Per the spec:
"The name of each explicitly specified method must be unique and not
blank."

Example:
type T interface {
_(int)
}

title: Incomparable Map Key
description:
Official Go type-checker code. IncomparableMapKey occurs when a map key type does not support the == and
!= operators.

Per the spec:
"The comparison operators == and != must be fully defined for operands of
the key type; thus the key type must not be a function, map, or slice."

Example:
var x map[T]int

type T []int

title: Invalid Ptr Embed
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidPtrEmbed occurs when an embedded field is of the pointer form *T,
and T itself is itself a pointer, an unsafe.Pointer, or an interface.

Per the spec:
"An embedded field must be specified as a type name T or as a pointer to
a non-interface type name *T, and T itself may not be a pointer type."

Example:
type T *int

type S struct {
*T
}

title: Bad Recv
description:
Official Go type-checker code. BadRecv occurs when a method declaration does not have exactly one
receiver parameter.

Example:
func () _() {}

title: Invalid Recv
Duplicate Field And Method
Duplicate Method
Invalid Blank
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidBlank occurs when a blank identifier is used as a value or type.

Per the spec:
"The blank identifier may appear as an operand only on the left-hand side
of an assignment."

Example:
var x = _

title: Invalid Iota
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidIota occurs when the predeclared identifier iota is used outside
of a constant declaration.

Example:
var x = iota

title: Missing Init Body
Invalid Init Sig
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidInitSig occurs when an init function declares parameters or
results.

Deprecated: no longer emitted by the type checker. _InvalidInitDecl is
used instead.

title: Invalid Init Decl
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidInitDecl occurs when init is declared as anything other than a
function.

Example:
var init = 1

Example:
func init() int { return 1 }

title: Invalid Main Decl
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidMainDecl occurs when main is declared as anything other than a
function, in a main package.

title: Too Many Values
Not An Expr
Truncated Float
description:
Official Go type-checker code. TruncatedFloat occurs when a float constant is truncated to an integer
value.

Example:
var _ int = 98.6

title: Numeric Overflow
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NumericOverflow occurs when a numeric constant overflows its target type.

Example:
var x int8 = 1000

title: Undefined Op
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UndefinedOp occurs when an operator is not defined for the type(s) used
in an operation.

Example:
var c = "a" - "b"

title: Mismatched Types
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MismatchedTypes occurs when operand types are incompatible in a binary
operation.

Example:
var a = "hello"
var b = 1
var c = a - b

title: Div By Zero
description:
Official Go type-checker code. DivByZero occurs when a division operation is provable at compile
time to be a division by zero.

Example:
const divisor = 0
var x int = 1/divisor

title: Non Numeric Inc Dec
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NonNumericIncDec occurs when an increment or decrement operator is
applied to a non-numeric value.

Example:
func f() {
var c = "c"
c++
}

title: Unaddressable Operand
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnaddressableOperand occurs when the & operator is applied to an
unaddressable expression.

Example:
var x = &1

title: Invalid Indirection
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidIndirection occurs when a non-pointer value is indirected via the
'*' operator.

Example:
var x int
var y = *x

title: Non Indexable Operand
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NonIndexableOperand occurs when an index operation is applied to a value
that cannot be indexed.

Example:
var x = 1
var y = x[1]

title: Invalid Index
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidIndex occurs when an index argument is not of integer type,
negative, or out-of-bounds.

Example:
var s = [...]int{1,2,3}
var x = s[5]

Example:
var s = []int{1,2,3}
var _ = s[-1]

Example:
var s = []int{1,2,3}
var i string
var _ = s[i]

title: Swapped Slice Indices
description:
Official Go type-checker code. SwappedSliceIndices occurs when constant indices in a slice expression
are decreasing in value.

Example:
var _ = []int{1,2,3}[2:1]

title: Non Sliceable Operand
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NonSliceableOperand occurs when a slice operation is applied to a value
whose type is not sliceable, or is unaddressable.

Example:
var x = [...]int{1, 2, 3}[:1]

Example:
var x = 1
var y = 1[:1]

title: Invalid Slice Expr
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidSliceExpr occurs when a three-index slice expression (a[x:y:z]) is
applied to a string.

Example:
var s = "hello"
var x = s[1:2:3]

title: Invalid Shift Count
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidShiftCount occurs when the right-hand side of a shift operation is
either non-integer, negative, or too large.

Example:
var (
x string
y int = 1 << x
)

title: Invalid Shift Operand
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidShiftOperand occurs when the shifted operand is not an integer.

Example:
var s = "hello"
var x = s << 2

title: Invalid Receive
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidReceive occurs when there is a channel receive from a value that
is either not a channel, or is a send-only channel.

Example:
func f() {
var x = 1
<-x
}

title: Invalid Send
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidSend occurs when there is a channel send to a value that is not a
channel, or is a receive-only channel.

Example:
func f() {
var x = 1
x <- "hello!"
}

title: Duplicate Lit Key
Missing Lit Key
Invalid Lit Index
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidLitIndex occurs when the key in a key-value element of a slice or
array literal is not an integer constant.

Example:
var i = 0
var x = []string{i: "world"}

title: Oversize Array Lit
Mixed Struct Lit
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MixedStructLit occurs when a struct literal contains a mix of positional
and named elements.

Example:
var _ = struct{i, j int}{i: 1, 2}

title: Invalid Struct Lit
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidStructLit occurs when a positional struct literal has an incorrect
number of values.

Example:
var _ = struct{i, j int}{1,2,3}

title: Missing Lit Field
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MissingLitField occurs when a struct literal refers to a field that does
not exist on the struct type.

Example:
var _ = struct{i int}{j: 2}

title: Duplicate Lit Field
description:
Official Go type-checker code. DuplicateLitField occurs when a struct literal contains duplicated
fields.

Example:
var _ = struct{i int}{i: 1, i: 2}

title: Unexported Lit Field
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnexportedLitField occurs when a positional struct literal implicitly
assigns an unexported field of an imported type.

title: Invalid Lit Field
Untyped Lit
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UntypedLit occurs when a composite literal omits a required type
identifier.

Example:
var _ = {}

title: Invalid Lit
Ambiguous Selector
Undeclared Imported Name
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UndeclaredImportedName occurs when a package-qualified identifier is
undeclared by the imported package.

Example:
import "go/types"

var _ = types.NotAnActualIdentifier

title: Unexported Name
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnexportedName occurs when a selector refers to an unexported identifier
of an imported package.

Example:
import "reflect"

type _ reflect.flag

title: Undeclared Name
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UndeclaredName occurs when an identifier is not declared in the current
scope.

Example:
var x T

title: Missing Field Or Method
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MissingFieldOrMethod occurs when a selector references a field or method
that does not exist.

Example:
type T struct {}

var x = T{}.f

title: Bad Dot Dot Dot Syntax
description:
Official Go type-checker code. BadDotDotDotSyntax occurs when a "..." occurs in a context where it is
not valid.

Example:
var _ = map[int][...]int{0: {}}

title: Non Variadic Dot Dot Dot
Invalid Dot Dot Dot
Uncalled Builtin
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UncalledBuiltin occurs when a built-in function is used as a
function-valued expression, instead of being called.

Per the spec:
"The built-in functions do not have standard Go types, so they can only
appear in call expressions; they cannot be used as function values."

Example:
var _ = copy

title: Invalid Append
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidAppend occurs when append is called with a first argument that is
not a slice.

Example:
var _ = append(1, 2)

title: Invalid Cap
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidCap occurs when an argument to the cap built-in function is not of
supported type.

See https://golang.org/ref/spec#Length_and_capacity for information on
which underlying types are supported as arguments to cap and len.

Example:
var s = 2
var x = cap(s)

title: Invalid Close
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidClose occurs when close(...) is called with an argument that is
not of channel type, or that is a receive-only channel.

Example:
func f() {
var x int
close(x)
}

title: Invalid Copy
Invalid Complex
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidComplex occurs when the complex built-in function is called with
arguments with incompatible types.

Example:
var _ = complex(float32(1), float64(2))

title: Invalid Delete
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidDelete occurs when the delete built-in function is called with a
first argument that is not a map.

Example:
func f() {
m := "hello"
delete(m, "e")
}

title: Invalid Imag
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidImag occurs when the imag built-in function is called with an
argument that does not have complex type.

Example:
var _ = imag(int(1))

title: Invalid Len
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidLen occurs when an argument to the len built-in function is not of
supported type.

See https://golang.org/ref/spec#Length_and_capacity for information on
which underlying types are supported as arguments to cap and len.

Example:
var s = 2
var x = len(s)

title: Swapped Make Args
description:
Official Go type-checker code. SwappedMakeArgs occurs when make is called with three arguments, and its
length argument is larger than its capacity argument.

Example:
var x = make([]int, 3, 2)

title: Invalid Make
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidMake occurs when make is called with an unsupported type argument.

See https://golang.org/ref/spec#Making_slices_maps_and_channels for
information on the types that may be created using make.

Example:
var x = make(int)

title: Invalid Real
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidReal occurs when the real built-in function is called with an
argument that does not have complex type.

Example:
var _ = real(int(1))

title: Invalid Assert
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidAssert occurs when a type assertion is applied to a
value that is not of interface type.

Example:
var x = 1
var _ = x.(float64)

title: Impossible Assert
Invalid Conversion
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidConversion occurs when the argument type cannot be converted to the
target.

See https://golang.org/ref/spec#Conversions for the rules of
convertibility.

Example:
var x float64
var _ = string(x)

title: Invalid Untyped Conversion
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidUntypedConversion occurs when there is no valid implicit
conversion from an untyped value satisfying the type constraints of the
context in which it is used.

Example:
func f[T ~int8 | ~int16 | ~int32 | ~int64](x T) T {
return x + 1024
}

title: Bad Offsetof Syntax
description:
Official Go type-checker code. BadOffsetofSyntax occurs when unsafe.Offsetof is called with an argument
that is not a selector expression.

Example:
import "unsafe"

var x int
var _ = unsafe.Offsetof(x)

title: Invalid Offsetof
Unused Expr
Unused Var
Missing Return
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MissingReturn occurs when a function with results is missing a return
statement.

Example:
func f() int {}

title: Wrong Result Count
Out Of Scope Result
Invalid Cond
Invalid Post Decl
Invalid Iter Var
Invalid Range Expr
Misplaced Break
Misplaced Continue
Misplaced Fallthrough
Duplicate Case
Duplicate Default
Bad Type Keyword
Invalid Type Switch
Invalid Expr Switch
Invalid Select Case
Undeclared Label
Duplicate Label
description:
Official Go type-checker code. DuplicateLabel occurs when a label is declared more than once.

Example:
func f() int {
L:
L:
return 1
}

title: Misplaced Label
Unused Label
Jump Over Decl
description:
Official Go type-checker code. JumpOverDecl occurs when a label jumps over a variable declaration.

Example:
func f() int {
goto L
x := 2
L:
x++
return x
}

title: Jump Into Block
Invalid Method Expr
Wrong Arg Count
Invalid Call
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidCall occurs when an expression is called that is not of function
type.

Example:
var x = "x"
var y = x()

title: Unused Results
description:
Official Go type-checker code. UnusedResults occurs when a restricted expression-only built-in function
is suspended via go or defer. Such a suspension discards the results of
these side-effect free built-in functions, and therefore is ineffectual.

Example:
func f(a []int) int {
defer len(a)
return i
}

title: Invalid Defer
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidDefer occurs when a deferred expression is not a function call,
for example if the expression is a type conversion.

Example:
func f(i int) int {
defer int32(i)
return i
}

title: Invalid Go
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidGo occurs when a go expression is not a function call, for example
if the expression is a type conversion.

Example:
func f(i int) int {
go int32(i)
return i
}

title: Bad Decl
description:
Official Go type-checker code. All codes below were added in Go 1.17.

BadDecl occurs when a declaration has invalid syntax.

title: Repeated Decl
Invalid Unsafe Add
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidUnsafeAdd occurs when unsafe.Add is called with a
length argument that is not of integer type.
It also occurs if it is used in a package compiled for a
language version before go1.17.

Example:
import "unsafe"

var p unsafe.Pointer
var _ = unsafe.Add(p, float64(1))

title: Invalid Unsafe Slice
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidUnsafeSlice occurs when unsafe.Slice is called with a
pointer argument that is not of pointer type or a length argument
that is not of integer type, negative, or out of bounds.
It also occurs if it is used in a package compiled for a language
version before go1.17.

Example:
import "unsafe"

var x int
var _ = unsafe.Slice(x, 1)

Example:
import "unsafe"

var x int
var _ = unsafe.Slice(&x, float64(1))

Example:
import "unsafe"

var x int
var _ = unsafe.Slice(&x, -1)

Example:
import "unsafe"

var x int
var _ = unsafe.Slice(&x, uint64(1) << 63)

title: Unsupported Feature
description:
Official Go type-checker code. All codes below were added in Go 1.18.

UnsupportedFeature occurs when a language feature is used that is not
supported at this Go version.

title: Not A Generic Type
description:
Official Go type-checker code. NotAGenericType occurs when a non-generic type is used where a generic
type is expected: in type or function instantiation.

Example:
type T int

var _ T[int]

title: Wrong Type Arg Count
description:
Official Go type-checker code. WrongTypeArgCount occurs when a type or function is instantiated with an
incorrect number of type arguments, including when a generic type or
function is used without instantiation.

Errors involving failed type inference are assigned other error codes.

Example:
type T[p any] int

var _ T[int, string]

Example:
func f[T any]() {}

var x = f

title: Cannot Infer Type Args
Invalid Type Arg
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidTypeArg occurs when a type argument does not satisfy its
corresponding type parameter constraints.

Example:
type T[P ~int] struct{}

var _ T[string]

title: Invalid Instance Cycle
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidInstanceCycle occurs when an invalid cycle is detected
within the instantiation graph.

Example:
func f[T any]() { f[*T]() }

title: Invalid Union
Misplaced Constraint Iface
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MisplacedConstraintIface occurs when a constraint-type interface is used
outside of constraint position.

Example:
type I interface { ~int }

var _ I

title: Invalid Method Type Params
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidMethodTypeParams occurs when methods have type parameters.

It cannot be encountered with an AST parsed using go/parser.

title: Misplaced Type Param
description:
Official Go type-checker code. MisplacedTypeParam occurs when a type parameter is used in a place where
it is not permitted.

Example:
type T[P any] P

Example:
type T[P any] struct{ *P }

title: Invalid Unsafe Slice Data
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidUnsafeSliceData occurs when unsafe.SliceData is called with
an argument that is not of slice type. It also occurs if it is used
in a package compiled for a language version before go1.20.

Example:
import "unsafe"

var x int
var _ = unsafe.SliceData(x)

title: Invalid Unsafe String
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidUnsafeString occurs when unsafe.String is called with
a length argument that is not of integer type, negative, or
out of bounds. It also occurs if it is used in a package
compiled for a language version before go1.20.

Example:
import "unsafe"

var b [10]byte
var _ = unsafe.String(&b[0], -1)

title: Invalid Clear
Type Too Large
description:
Official Go type-checker code. TypeTooLarge occurs if unsafe.Sizeof or unsafe.Offsetof is
called with an expression whose type is too large.

Example:
import "unsafe"

type E [1 << 31 - 1]int
var a [1 << 31]E
var _ = unsafe.Sizeof(a)

Example:
import "unsafe"

type E [1 << 31 - 1]int
var s struct {
_ [1 << 31]E
x int
}
var _ = unsafe.Offsetof(s.x)

title: Invalid Min Max Operand
description:
Official Go type-checker code. InvalidMinMaxOperand occurs if min or max is called
with an operand that cannot be ordered because it
does not support the < operator.

Example:
const _ = min(true)

Example:
var s, t []byte
var _ = max(s, t)

title: Too New
description:
Official Go type-checker code. TooNew indicates that, through build tags or a go.mod file,
a source file requires a version of Go that is newer than
the logic of the type checker. As a consequence, the type
checker may produce spurious errors or fail to report real
errors. The solution is to rebuild the application with a
newer Go release.
